chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: Conversion narratives run in opposing directions and can accompany reported improvements in values and meaning, so their existence alone supplies little net evidence for Christianity.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of any retained opposing move, the documented existence of beneficial reverse-conversion narratives establishes an evidential symmetry that cautions against inferring Christianity from conversion testimony alone.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Across billions of lives, culturally familiar conversion scripts and ordinary coincidences can naturally generate apparently coordinated conversion stories without supernatural causation.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a standalone naturalistic explanation, population size, familiar cultural narratives, and ordinary coincidence make the occurrence of some detailed conversion stories unsurprising without providential intervention.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: Even the strongest arguments on both sides fail to compel a unique verdict, leaving both theistic and atheistic positions rationally permissible.

orphanFallback.rationale: This independently states the governing epistemic standard: rational permissibility may persist when the total argumentative case does not force rational convergence on either theism or atheism.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Persistent disagreement among expert philosophers of religion indicates that neither theistic nor atheistic arguments compel rational convergence, even after sustained inquiry.

orphanFallback.rationale: Standing alone, the continuing division among accomplished specialists supports epistemic caution by showing that greater expertise has not disclosed a decisive argument forcing either conclusion.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Naturalism has a structurally parallel cumulative case, while arguments from evil and divine hiddenness require theists to identify which premises they reject and accept the resulting commitments.

orphanFallback.rationale: As an independent constructive point, evil and divine hiddenness are serious considerations within a cumulative naturalist case and impose substantive explanatory obligations on theism.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: The cultural and historical diversity of religious experiences and their interpretations substantially weakens testimonial support for Christianity specifically.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently presented, the tendency of reported experiences to track inherited cultural concepts rather than converge on Jesus supplies a naturalistic reason to discount their specifically Christian evidential force.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Comparative assessment of Christianity and Islam requires substantial expertise, and the available historical record does not plainly establish a stronger case for Christianity.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a standalone caution, greater recency supplies substantial information about early Islam, while comparatively limited knowledge of earliest Christianity prevents an easy historical advantage for Christianity.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Christianity's larger surviving documentary record partly reflects later institutional dominance and selective preservation, so document quantity alone is not compelling evidence of historical superiority.

orphanFallback.rationale: Independently of a retained documentary claim, the source describes a preservation mechanism by which Christian dominance increased Christian document survival and reduced the evidential significance of raw quantity.
